newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rebound on Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rebound on Greenspan comments.

text.p: Stock prices powered higher Wednesday after Wall Street put a positive spin on the latest remarks by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan ahead of his Congressional testimony scheduled for later in the day.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 29.25 points at 6,881.97, recovering from Tuesday's late sell-off of 66 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 13-9 on active volume of 288 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Analysts also said a bounce was probably inevitable after the beating taken by many blue-chip stocks on Tuesday. But they questioned how far the market could run ahead of Friday's February employment report.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was flat and its yield held at Tuesday's close of 6.87 percent.
Speaking to the National Association of Business Economists, Greenspan defended his cautionary comments, which sparked a stock slide last week and again denied he was trying to talk the market lower.
Greenspan rattled Wall Street first in December, then again last week after he suggested that stocks might have risen too far on account of investors' "irrational exuberance."
On Tuesday morning, he said the market was properly priced if Wall Street analysts' earnings estimates were correct.

"I think he is saying that it is okay to be exuberant as long as everything turns out exactly as people expect," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. "I believe that he was taken aback by the reaction to his comments, which I believe were very courageous."
Greenspan will present the second half of his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony before the House of Representatives at 2 p.m. EST (1900 GMT).
"His comments are what influenced market action today," said Anthony O'Bryan, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons.
He said the comments that Greenspan made about stock market valuations being correct if earnings lived up to expectations were positive.

"If Wall Street did not believe earnings would live up to expectations, the market would not be where it is now," he said. "His remarks lifted some of the tension concerning this afternoon's testimony. He is unlikely to take a tougher position later today. By talking early and taking a tactful approach, he has calmed the waters."
But analysts said that the rally was not very convincing as the bond market barely participated.
Among the big movers, Corporate Express Inc. lost 8-7/16 to 9-7/8 after the company warned that its quarterly results would not meet Wall Street expectations.
Also down sharply was Broderbund Software Inc., off 7-1/4 at 23-1/4 after the company also warned of disappointing profits.

Boeing Co. rose 3-1/8 at 103-3/8 on news late Tuesday that it expected the world's airlines would add more than 16,000 new jets worth $1.1 trillion over the next 20 years, driven by strong growth in Asia-Pacific market.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 5.67 to 1,323.04. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.72 to 599.76.
